# INC-0001: Autogenerated vocabulary migrations were empty

## Signature
```
sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (asyncpg.exceptions.UndefinedTableError) relation "search_terms" does not exist
```
`alembic current` reports head `da03da123834`, but `\dt search_terms` finds nothing.

## Summary
Two Alembic revisions that were meant to add the vocabulary tables, `4f9fab47f6a0` ("add search terms table", 2026-10-30) and `da03da123834` ("vocabulary state model added", 2026-10-30), have `upgrade()` and `downgrade()` bodies that only contain `pass`. Running `alembic upgrade head` stamped them as applied and created nothing. The PR #3 writer code then ran against a database with no `search_terms` table, so any index write that changed terms would fail. Code review of PR #3 caught it before it caused data loss.

> **Question for nish:** did this break a real indexer run on your machine, or was it only caught in review? If it broke a run, paste the actual error here and set the severity accordingly.

## Expected vs actual
- Expected: `alembic revision --autogenerate` after adding `SearchTerm` and `VocabularyDocumentState` produces `op.create_table(...)` for both tables.
- Actual: both generated revisions were empty, and nobody noticed before they were committed and applied.

## Root cause
Autogenerate compares the database against `Base.metadata`. `backend/alembic/env.py` fills that metadata with `import backend.models`, and `backend/src/backend/models/__init__.py` imports only `CrawlAttempt`, `CrawlTarget`, `Document`, `RobotsCache`, `SearchIndex`, `Source`, `CrawlEvent` and `CrawlWorker`. `search_terms.py` and `vocabulary_document_state.py` were never imported, so their tables were not in the metadata and Alembic saw no difference. This is still true at `a756c10`.

## Fixes that did not work
| Attempt | Why it failed |
| --- | --- |
| Editing the bodies of `4f9fab47f6a0` / `da03da123834` | Databases that already ran them are stamped past those revisions and would never run the new body. |

> **Question for nish:** is this table right? If you tried something else first (re-running autogenerate, creating the table by hand), add it.

## Resolution
PR #4 (`c0d1690`) added a new forward revision, `9a71c3fb20d4_ensure_search_terms`, after `da03da123834`. It runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.search_terms (...)` with both check constraints, and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_search_terms_trgm ... USING gin (term gin_trgm_ops)`. Fresh databases and databases already stamped at `da03da123834` both end up with the table. `downgrade()` is a no-op so it cannot drop a table someone created by hand before the repair.

This is marked **mitigated, not resolved**, because the root cause is still there:
- `backend/models/__init__.py` still does not import `SearchTerm` or `VocabularyDocumentState`, so the next autogenerate will either miss changes to those models again or, once they are imported, try to create `search_terms` a second time.
- `vocabulary_document_state` has a model but no migration and no code that uses it.
- `IF NOT EXISTS` does not check that an existing `search_terms` table has the right columns.

## Prevention
- Regression test: none yet. A cheap one is a test that imports `backend.models` and asserts every table name defined under `backend/models/` is in `Base.metadata.tables`, or a CI step that runs `alembic check` against a migrated database.
- Monitoring: none.
- Design change: none.
- Remaining risk: any new model file that is not added to `models/__init__.py` repeats this incident.

## Rules for future changes
- Every new model must be imported in `backend/src/backend/models/__init__.py` before running `alembic revision --autogenerate`.
- Read every autogenerated revision before committing it. An `upgrade()` that is only `pass` is a bug unless the message says it is intentionally empty.
- Never edit a revision that may already be applied. Add a new forward revision.
